theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Before starting a job with hand and power tools, what should you do first?
options: Read the job instructions or drawing and plan the steps
Pick up the nearest tool and start cutting at once
Ask a co-worker to do the hardest part for you
Switch on all the power tools to warm them up

questions.stem: Why must you choose the right tool for each job?
options: So that the toolbox always looks neat and full of tools
It does the job safely and does not damage the work
So you use every tool at least once each day
Any tool will do if you push hard enough

questions.stem: Shanice picks up a screwdriver with a cracked handle. What should she do?
options: Wrap tape tightly around the crack and use it carefully
Not use it; label it faulty and tell the supervisor
Use it only for the small, easy screws on the job
Put it back in the toolbox for someone else

questions.stem: Which check should you make on a hammer before using it?
options: That the handle is painted a bright colour
That the head is shiny and newly polished
That the head is tight and the handle is not split
That it is the heaviest hammer in the shop

questions.stem: What eye protection should you wear when using an angle grinder?
options: Your own glasses, if you normally wear them
None, as long as you stand well back from it
A pair of reading glasses or ordinary sunglasses
Safety goggles with a face shield over them

questions.stem: Why should long hair be tied back and loose clothing tucked in when using a power drill?
options: So you look neat and tidy for the customer
So the drill does not overheat
So nothing gets caught in the turning parts
So you can work faster without stopping

questions.stem: When should you wear ear protection?
options: When using loud tools such as grinders
Only when the supervisor is in the workshop
Only when working alone at the end of the day
Never, because noise does no lasting harm to ears

questions.stem: A worker is cutting steel with an angle grinder. Where should the sparks be pointed?
options: Towards the doorway so that they fly outside
Away from people and anything that can burn
Towards the worker's feet to keep them low
Into a cardboard box so they are all caught

questions.stem: Which item of PPE protects you from breathing in fine dust when sanding or cutting concrete?
options: A clear plastic face shield
Leather gloves
A dust mask or respirator
Ear muffs

questions.stem: Which tool would you use to scratch a fine, sharp line on steel before cutting it?
options: A pencil
A wax crayon
A scriber
A screwdriver

questions.stem: Andre must cut a piece of flat bar 250 mm long. Why should he measure from a squared, clean end?
options: So that the measurement starts from a true edge
So that the steel rule does not get scratched or rusty
So the bar is lighter to carry
So the hacksaw blade lasts longer

questions.stem: Which way should the teeth of a hacksaw blade point when it is fitted to the frame?
options: Forward, away from the handle
Backward, towards the handle
Up, towards the top of the frame
Either way, it makes no difference

questions.stem: Which hacksaw blade is best for cutting thin-walled steel tube?
options: 14 TPI (coarse)
32 TPI (fine)
18 TPI (medium)
Any blade, as long as it is new

questions.stem: Why should at least three teeth of a hacksaw blade be touching the work at all times?
options: So the cut is made at an angle
So the teeth do not catch and break off
So the blade gets hot and cuts faster
So the work does not need to be held in a vice

questions.stem: How should you use a hacksaw to get the best cut?
options: Short fast strokes using just the middle of the blade
Press down hard on both the push and the pull
Long steady strokes, pressing only on the push
Twist the frame from side to side as you cut

questions.stem: Kemar's hacksaw blade snaps in the middle of a cut. Which is a likely cause?
options: The blade had its teeth pointing forward
The blade was loose or he twisted the saw
He used long strokes and gentle pressure
The work was held firmly in a vice

questions.stem: Why must a file always have a handle fitted?
options: So the pointed tang cannot stab your hand
So that the file will cut on both of its strokes
So the file can be used as a lever
So that the file does not get rusty

questions.stem: Which of these files removes metal the fastest?
options: Bastard cut
Second cut
Smooth cut
Dead smooth cut

questions.stem: What is "draw filing" used for?
options: Cutting a groove across the end of a bar
Marking the centre of a hole before drilling
Sharpening a drill bit by hand
Giving a smooth, flat finish along an edge

questions.stem: Which hammer is best for driving and pulling nails in timber?
options: Ball pein hammer
Sledge hammer
Cross pein hammer
Claw hammer

questions.stem: What should be done with a cold chisel whose head has spread out and cracked from use?
options: Keep using it, as the cutting edge is still sharp
Paint the head so the cracks do not show
Grind the head smooth or replace the chisel
Hit it harder so the cracks close up

questions.stem: Why should you never strike two hardened hammer faces together?
options: It makes the hammers too heavy to lift
It will loosen the wooden handles
It makes a noise that upsets customers
Chips of steel can fly off and cause injury

questions.stem: What happens if you use a screwdriver tip that is too small for the screw?
options: The screw goes in faster and tighter
The screwdriver gets longer with use
The tip slips and damages the screw head
The screw will need no further tightening

questions.stem: Why is a ring spanner better than an open-ended spanner on a very tight nut?
options: It grips all the corners, so it is less likely to slip
It is lighter, so it can be turned more quickly
It can be used on any size of nut without changing
It is strong enough to be hit with a hammer to free nuts

questions.stem: Delroy cannot undo a tight, rusty nut with a spanner. What is the safe way to go on?
options: Slide a long pipe over the spanner for more force
Hit the spanner with a hammer until it moves
Use a pair of pliers, as they grip harder than spanners
Use penetrating oil, wait, then try the right spanner

questions.stem: Why should pliers not be used to turn nuts and bolts?
options: Pliers are much too short to reach most of the nuts
Pliers are only made for cutting timber
Pliers turn nuts the wrong way round
They slip and round off the corners of the nut

questions.stem: Why should work be held firmly in a vice when sawing or filing?
options: So the tool can be held in one hand
So it cannot move, slip or vibrate
So you do not need to wear gloves
So the work cools down more quickly

questions.stem: Marsha needs to hold a polished brass part in a vice without marking it. What should she use?
options: Soft jaws or clamp pads made of aluminium or fibre
Extra force on the vice handle with a hammer
Rough sandpaper placed between the jaws
A thick layer of grease spread on the vice jaws

questions.stem: What should you check on a power tool's cable and plug before use?
options: That the cable is long enough to reach anywhere
That the plug matches the colour of the tool
That any cuts in the cable have been taped up
No cuts, burns, bare wires or loose plug pins

questions.stem: Why should you unplug a power tool before changing a disc, blade or drill bit?
options: So the tool cannot start by accident
So that the new disc fits more tightly
So that the motor cools down faster
So the cable does not get tangled

questions.stem: A cable reel (an extension lead on a drum) is used for a power tool. Why should all of the cable be unwound?
options: So the tool will run at a higher speed
So nobody can trip over the cable
So the coiled cable does not overheat
So the reel is lighter to carry

questions.stem: Odane notices that the drill's casing is cracked and the drill feels hot in one spot. What should he do?
options: Finish the hole quickly, then report it later
Wrap some tape around the crack and carry on working
Stop, unplug it, tag it as faulty and report it
Pour some water on the casing to cool it down

questions.stem: Why must power tools be kept away from water and wet floors?
options: Water makes the tool too heavy to use
Water washes the grease off the cable
Water makes the tool run more slowly
Water can cause an electric shock

questions.stem: Before fitting a disc to an angle grinder, what must you check on the disc?
options: That its colour is the same as the grinder's
That it is the thickest disc in the whole store
That its speed rating is not below the grinder's
That it is a little bigger than the guard

questions.stem: Why should a thin cutting disc not be used to grind with its flat side?
options: It is not made for side loads and can shatter
It will cut too quickly and waste the steel
It makes the grinder run backwards
It leaves a finish that is hard to paint

questions.stem: How should an angle grinder be held when cutting?
options: In one hand, so the other can hold the work
Loosely, so it can find its own path
Pressed against your leg or body for extra support
Firmly with both hands, using the side handle

questions.stem: When you finish a cut with an angle grinder, what should you do before putting it down?
options: Put it down at once, spinning, to save time
Hold the disc with a glove to slow it down
Press the disc on the bench to stop it
Switch off and wait for the disc to stop

questions.stem: Before drilling a hole in a small piece of steel with a portable drill, what should you do with the work?
options: Hold it in your hand so you can feel the drill
Stand on it to keep it still
Clamp it firmly or hold it in a vice
Put it on the floor and kneel on it

questions.stem: Which drill bit should be used to drill a hole in mild steel?
options: A masonry bit with a carbide tip
A high-speed steel (HSS) twist bit
A flat spade bit made for timber
A spear-point bit for glass and tile

questions.stem: Ricardo must drill a 12 mm hole in steel plate with a portable drill. What is good practice?
options: Drill at top speed with heavy force and no pilot hole
Lean all your weight on the drill to get through fast
Use a blunt bit so that it does not grab
Drill a small pilot hole first, then open it up

questions.stem: For a drill with a keyed chuck, what must you do before switching it on?
options: Remove the chuck key from the chuck
Wrap the cable around your arm
Hold the bit to check it is tight
Put on loose gloves for grip

questions.stem: Before changing the blade on a battery-powered jigsaw, what should you do?
options: Switch it to the slowest speed
Take the battery out of the tool
Lock the trigger in the on position
Put the tool on charge

questions.stem: On a hand-held circular saw, what should the lower blade guard do?
options: Stay wedged open so you can see the blade
Be taken off so that the saw cuts faster
Spring back to cover the blade after the cut
Stay fixed half way down the blade at all times

questions.stem: How should hand tools be stored at the end of the day?
options: Left on the bench, ready for the morning
Cleaned and put back in their proper place
Thrown together in one box to save room
Taken home by the last worker to use them

questions.stem: Why should steel hand tools be wiped with a lightly oiled cloth before they are stored?
options: To make them slippery and harder to steal
To stop them rusting in the damp sea air
To make them look new for the customers
To make the handles grip better next time

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What do we call a hammer with a soft head of rubber, plastic or wood, used so that the work is not marked?
What is the name of the stiff wire brush used to clean metal bits out of the teeth of a file?
What do the letters TPI stand for on a hacksaw blade?
What do the letters PPE stand for?

What is the name of the electrical safety device that cuts off the power very quickly if current leaks to earth, to protect a person from shock?

What is the name of the tool used to check that two surfaces of a piece of steel are at 90° to each other?
What is the name of the flat steel measuring tool marked in millimetres, often 300 mm long?
What do we call removing the sharp, rough edge left on metal after cutting or drilling?

On a power tool, a symbol of one square inside another square means the tool is what?

essays.stem: Describe how you would plan and prepare for a small job using hand and power tools, such as cutting and drilling a steel bracket.
essays.modelAnswer: First I read the drawing or job sheet and check the sizes, the material and how many pieces are needed. I plan the steps in order: measure and mark, cut, file, drill and finish. Then I choose the right tool for each step, for example a steel rule, square and scriber for marking, a hacksaw or angle grinder for cutting, files, a centre punch and a drill with the right size HSS bit. I collect the material and check it is the right size and not damaged. I check each tool before use: handles tight, blades sharp, cables and plugs undamaged and guards in place. I put on the PPE needed, such as safety glasses and boots, plus ear protection and a face shield for the grinder. I set up a clean, clear work area with a vice or clamps to hold the work, and check where sparks will go. If anything is unclear, I ask my supervisor before I start.
markingPoints: Reads the drawing or job sheet and checks sizes and material
Plans the steps in a sensible order
Chooses the right tool for each step and checks the material
Checks each tool before use (handles, blades, cables, plugs, guards)
Puts on the right PPE, sets up a safe area, and asks if unsure

essays.stem: Describe the PPE you would wear when using an angle grinder, and say what each item protects you against.
essays.modelAnswer: Safety glasses or goggles protect the eyes from sparks, chips and broken pieces of disc. A full face shield worn over them protects the whole face as well, because grinding throws particles out at high speed. Ear muffs or ear plugs protect my hearing from the loud noise, which can cause lasting damage over time. Leather gloves that fit well protect my hands from sparks, hot metal and sharp edges. Long sleeves and long trousers of cotton or a flame-resistant material protect my skin from sparks. Nylon and polyester should not be worn, as they can melt onto the skin. Safety boots protect my feet from falling steel and hot pieces. A dust mask or respirator protects my lungs when grinding painted or galvanised steel or in a dusty area. Long hair is tied back and loose items are removed so nothing can be caught by the disc.
markingPoints: Safety glasses or goggles with a face shield: sparks, chips, disc fragments
Ear protection: noise that can damage hearing
Leather gloves: sparks, heat and sharp edges
Flame-resistant long sleeves and trousers (not nylon or polyester) and safety boots
Dust mask or respirator where there is dust or coated steel

essays.stem: Explain the checks you would make on a portable electric power tool and its extension lead before use, and what you would do if you found a fault.
essays.modelAnswer: First I check that the tool has a current test tag or inspection mark, if the Centre uses them. I look along the whole cable for cuts, burns, crushed spots or tape, and check that the outer cover goes right into the plug and the tool, with no coloured wires showing. I check the plug for cracks, bent or loose pins and signs of burning. I check the casing for cracks and that all the screws are in place. I check that the switch moves freely and turns the tool off, and that any guard, side handle and the disc, blade or bit are fitted, of the right type and in good condition. I check the extension lead in the same way and unwind it fully. If I find any fault, I do not use the tool. I unplug it, put a "Do not use" tag on it, keep it apart from the good tools and report it to my supervisor. I never try to repair an electrical fault myself.
markingPoints: Checks the test tag or inspection mark
Checks the cable and plug: no cuts, burns, tape, bare wires or loose pins
Checks the casing, switch, guard, handle and accessory
Checks the extension lead the same way and unwinds it fully
If faulty: do not use, unplug, tag, separate and report; no home-made repairs

essays.stem: Describe how to fit a new blade to a hacksaw, and how to make a straight cut in a piece of steel flat bar.
essays.modelAnswer: To fit a new blade, I loosen the wing nut, take out the old blade and choose the right new one: a finer blade for thin material and a coarser one for thick, so that at least three teeth touch the work. I fit it with the teeth pointing forward, away from the handle, and tighten the wing nut until the blade is tight and does not twist. To cut, I mark the cutting line around the bar with a scriber and square. I hold the bar firmly in the vice with the line close to the jaws, so it does not vibrate. I start the cut gently on the waste side of the line, using a small nick made with a file to guide the blade. Then I use long, steady strokes, using most of the blade, pressing on the forward stroke and easing off on the return. I keep the frame upright and watch the line on both sides. Near the end I slow down and support the offcut so it does not fall. Finally I remove the burrs.
markingPoints: Chooses a blade to suit the thickness (at least three teeth on the work)
Fits the blade with teeth forward and tensions it
Marks the line and holds the bar firmly in the vice close to the cut
Starts on the waste side; long steady strokes, pressure on the forward stroke only
Slows at the end, supports the offcut and deburrs

essays.stem: Explain how to file the end of a steel bar flat and square, and how to look after files.
essays.modelAnswer: I hold the bar firmly in the vice, with the end to be filed just above the jaws so it does not vibrate. I check that the file has a tight handle. I use a coarse file, such as a bastard cut, to remove metal, then a second cut or smooth file to finish. I stand with my feet apart, one hand on the handle and the other near the tip, and push the file straight forward across the work with even pressure. I ease off on the return stroke, because a file cuts only on the forward stroke. I keep the file level and change its direction from time to time so I can see the high spots. I check often with a try square against the side of the bar, holding it up to the light, until no light shows. To look after files, I clean them with a file card, keep them dry, store them apart so the teeth do not rub together, and never use a file as a lever or a hammer.
markingPoints: Holds the work firmly in the vice, close to the jaws
File has a tight handle; coarse file first, then a finer one
Correct stance; pushes forward with even pressure and eases off on the return
Keeps the file level and checks with a try square against the light
Care: file card, kept dry, stored apart, never used as a lever or hammer

essays.stem: Describe how to change the disc on an angle grinder safely and then use it to cut a piece of steel.
essays.modelAnswer: First I unplug the grinder, or take out its battery. I check that the new disc is a cutting disc of the right size for the grinder, undamaged and within its use-by date, and that its speed rating is not lower than the grinder's speed. I press the spindle lock, undo the flange nut with the correct key, fit the disc the right way round and tighten the nut. I check that the guard is fitted and set between the disc and me, and that the side handle is fitted. I clamp the work firmly, with the cut line over the edge of the bench, and make sure the sparks will go away from people, gas cylinders and anything that can burn. Wearing goggles, a face shield, ear protection, gloves and suitable clothing, I plug in and run the grinder for a moment, pointed away from others, to check it runs smoothly. I hold it with both hands and cut with light, steady pressure, keeping the disc straight in the cut. When I finish, I switch off and let the disc stop before putting the grinder down.
markingPoints: Unplugs the grinder (or removes the battery) before changing the disc
Checks the disc: type, size, condition and speed rating
Fits the disc correctly; guard and side handle in place
Clamps the work and controls where the sparks go; wears the right PPE
Test runs, uses both hands, keeps the disc straight, and lets it stop before putting it down

essays.stem: Describe how to mark out and drill an accurate 10 mm hole in a steel plate using a portable drill.
essays.modelAnswer: I read the drawing to find where the hole goes. I scribe two lines with a rule and square so they cross at the centre of the hole. Then I make a small dent with a centre punch exactly where the lines cross, so the drill does not wander. I clamp the plate firmly to the bench or hold it in a vice, with a piece of scrap wood under it so I do not drill into the bench. I choose a sharp 10 mm HSS twist bit and a smaller pilot bit, about 4 to 5 mm. I fit each one tightly in the chuck and remove the chuck key. Wearing safety glasses, with sleeves and hair secured, I drill the pilot hole first, holding the drill square to the work, with steady pressure and a little cutting fluid. Then I open the hole with the 10 mm bit at a slower speed. I ease off as the bit breaks through. I let the drill stop, then deburr both sides and check the size and position of the hole.
markingPoints: Marks the centre with crossing lines and a centre punch
Clamps the work securely, with packing underneath
Chooses HSS bits, drills a pilot hole first, removes the chuck key
Wears eye protection; holds the drill square, uses steady pressure, cutting fluid and a slower speed for the large bit
Eases off at break-through, deburrs, and checks size and position

essays.stem: Compare hand tools and power tools. Give two advantages and two disadvantages of each, with examples.
essays.modelAnswer: Hand tools, such as hacksaws, files, chisels and spanners, are cheap, light and easy to carry. They need no electricity, so they can be used anywhere, even in a power cut or on a site with no supply. They also give good control for small, careful jobs. Their disadvantages are that they are slow and tiring on big jobs, and the result depends a lot on the worker's skill and strength. Power tools, such as angle grinders, electric drills and circular saws, work much faster and with less effort, so large jobs are finished sooner and often more evenly. Their disadvantages are that they cost more and need electricity or charged batteries. They are also more dangerous, with risks of electric shock, flying sparks and pieces, noise, dust and serious cuts, so they need more checks and maintenance. A good worker chooses the right tool for each job and often uses both.
markingPoints: Two advantages of hand tools (cheap, portable, no power needed, good control)
Two disadvantages of hand tools (slow, tiring, depends on skill)
Two advantages of power tools (faster, less effort, even results)
Two disadvantages of power tools (cost, need power, more hazards and maintenance)
Suitable examples of each kind of tool

essays.stem: Explain how hand and power tools should be cleaned, maintained and stored, and why this matters.
essays.modelAnswer: After use I clean each tool, brushing off dust, chips and filings and wiping off grease. Steel tools are wiped with a lightly oiled cloth so they do not rust in the damp, salty air. Cutting tools such as chisels and drill bits are kept sharp, or given to the person who sharpens them, because blunt tools need more force and slip more easily. Handles are checked, and loose or split ones are reported. For power tools, I unplug them or remove the battery, clean the air vents so the motor does not overheat, and coil the cable loosely without kinks rather than wrapping it tightly round the tool. Batteries are charged with the maker's charger. All tools go back in their proper place, such as a toolbox, rack or shadow board, so they are not damaged and missing tools are easy to see. Sharp edges are covered. This matters because well-kept tools are safer, last longer, do better work and save time.
markingPoints: Cleans tools after use and oils steel tools against rust
Keeps cutting tools sharp and checks handles
Power tools: unplugged, vents cleaned, cables coiled loosely, batteries charged with the maker's charger
Stores tools in their proper place with sharp edges covered
Why: safer, longer life, better work and less time wasted

essays.stem: Describe how you would keep the work area safe while using tools, and how you would clean up and report at the end of the job.
essays.modelAnswer: Before starting, I clear the area of rubbish and anything that can burn, and make sure walkways and exits are clear. I run cables where people will not trip, away from sharp edges, water and hot work. I put up screens when grinding so sparks and chips do not hit other people, and check that a fire extinguisher is close by. I keep only the tools I need on the bench and put the others away. I warn people nearby before starting a noisy or sparking tool. At the end of the job I switch off and unplug all power tools, let hot parts cool, and coil the leads. I sweep up filings, offcuts and dust, putting sharp offcuts and scrap in the scrap bin and rubbish in the right bin. I clean and return all the tools. I check the work against the drawing, then report to my supervisor that the job is done, along with any tool faults, damage or near misses.
markingPoints: Clears the area of rubbish and things that burn; keeps walkways clear
Runs cables safely away from trips, sharp edges, water and hot work
Uses screens, warns others and has a fire extinguisher near
At the end: switches off, unplugs, cools, coils leads, sweeps up and sorts scrap
Returns tools, checks the work and reports faults or near misses

practical1.title: Make a steel angle bracket using hand tools
practical1.brief: Each member of the group makes one steel angle bracket from 25 mm × 3 mm mild steel flat bar, to the assessor's drawing: a piece 150 mm long, bent to 90° at the middle, with one 8 mm hole in each leg. First, as a group, read the drawing together, check the tools and agree the order of work. Then each member: (1) measures and marks out the length with a steel rule, square and scriber; (2) cuts the bar to length with a hacksaw, with the bar held in the vice; (3) files both ends flat and square and removes the burrs; (4) marks and centre punches the hole centres; (5) drills the holes with a portable drill, with the bar clamped, drilling a pilot hole first; (6) bends the bar to 90° in the vice with a hammer and checks it with a square. Members take turns at the vice and the drill, and check each other's measurements. Photograph each stage and add the photos to the group's practical. Lay out all the brackets together for the final photo.
materials: One piece of 25 mm × 3 mm mild steel flat bar, about 160 mm long, for each member
The assessor's drawing of the bracket
Steel rule, try square, scriber and centre punch
Hacksaw with a suitable blade, flat files (bastard and second cut) and a file card
Ball pein hammer and a bench vice with soft jaws
Portable electric or battery drill, 4 mm and 8 mm HSS twist bits, and a G-clamp
Cutting fluid, and a deburring tool or small file
photos: The tools laid out and checked before starting, with the group in PPE
Bars marked out with the cut lines and hole centres
A member cutting a bar with the hacksaw, with the bar held in the vice
Ends filed square, with a try square held against one
Holes drilled and deburred, with the bar clamped for drilling
The brackets bent to 90° and checked with a square
All the finished brackets laid out next to the drawing
The work area cleaned and the tools put away
checklist: Wore safety glasses and safety boots throughout, with sleeves and hair secured
Checked the hand tools and the drill (handles, blade, cable, plug, chuck) before use
Marked out the length and hole centres accurately from the drawing
Fitted and used the hacksaw correctly, cutting close to the line
Filed the ends flat and square and removed all burrs
Clamped the work and drilled the pilot and final holes safely, with the chuck key removed
Bent the bracket to 90°, matching the drawing within its tolerance (about ±1 mm)
Cleaned and returned the tools, and swept up filings and offcuts
safety: Wear safety glasses at all times: chips and filings can fly when sawing, filing, drilling and hammering
Never hold the work in your hand while drilling: clamp it or use the vice
Check that hammer heads are tight and file handles are fitted before use
Keep the drill cable away from the bit and sharp edges, and unplug the drill before changing bits
Handle cut steel with care: the edges are sharp until deburred

practical2.title: Inspect, use and store portable power tools
practical2.brief: As a group, inspect a set of portable power tools, use them safely to cut and drill steel, and then store them correctly. The assessor sets out an angle grinder, a corded drill, a battery-powered drill and an extension lead, and one item has a fault. Stage 1: using the assessor's inspection form, each member inspects at least one item and fills in their part of the form. The group finds the faulty item, tags it "Do not use" and reports it to the assessor. Stage 2: each member in turn, watched by the assessor, checks and fits a cutting disc to the angle grinder with the grinder unplugged, cuts a piece of 25 mm × 25 mm × 3 mm steel angle to 200 mm long, then marks and drills a 6 mm hole 25 mm from one end with a portable drill. While one member works, another acts as spotter, keeping others clear and watching where the sparks go. Stage 3: the group cleans the tools, coils the leads, charges the battery with the maker's charger and stores everything in its proper place. Photograph each stage and add the photos to the group's practical.
materials: Angle grinder (115 mm or 125 mm) with cutting discs and the disc key
Corded electric drill, and a battery-powered drill with its charger
HSS twist bits (3 mm and 6 mm), centre punch and hammer
Lengths of 25 mm × 25 mm × 3 mm steel angle
Bench vice or G-clamps, steel rule, square and scriber
Inspection form, "Do not use" tags, screens and a fire extinguisher
photos: Each tool laid out for inspection with the inspection form
The faulty item tagged "Do not use"
A cutting disc being fitted with the grinder unplugged, showing the disc's speed rating
A member cutting the angle with a spotter and screens in place
A hole being drilled with the work clamped
The cut pieces with their lengths checked against a rule
The tools cleaned and stored, leads coiled and the battery on charge
checklist: Inspected their item fully (cable, plug, casing, switch, guard, accessory) and filled in the form correctly
Helped find, tag and report the faulty item
Unplugged the grinder before fitting the disc, and checked the disc's type, condition and speed rating
Wore goggles, face shield, ear protection, gloves and boots for grinding
Clamped the work, held the grinder with both hands and controlled the sparks
Cut the angle to 200 mm within about 2 mm and deburred the cut ends
Drilled the hole safely, with the work clamped and the bit on the punched mark
Let the disc stop before putting the grinder down
Cleaned, coiled and stored the tools correctly
safety: Unplug the tool, or remove its battery, before changing any disc, blade or bit
Use screens and keep a fire extinguisher at hand; point sparks away from people and anything that can burn
Never use a tool that has failed the inspection: tag it and report it
Keep the extension lead fully unwound and away from wet floors and walkways
Follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules for each tool
